answer_1.quote: In this paper, we consider mimicking fictional characters... We model a conversation agent that generates a response r corresponding to a given context x while mimicking an arbitrary character with k utterances {u1,…,uk} of the character.
answer_1.outputs: Generated conversational responses that aim to reflect the target character's style

answer_2.quote: Automatic Evaluation. Similar to the previous works on text style transfer, we utilize a character classifier... We denote StyleProb... For measuring coherency, we use MaUdE, an automated dialog evaluation metric... We also report n-gram overlap as an additional automated metric.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation to assess the quality of the generated responses. Using Amazon MTurk, we collect human annotations... Human evaluators are asked to rate from 0 to 2 scale score how each model response (1) strongly reveals the style of a given character (Style Strength) and (2) whether a response is fluent and appropriate for a given dialog context (Appropriateness).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each response on two criteria: Style Strength (how strongly the response reveals the target character's style) and Appropriateness (fluency and suitability to the dialog context).
